unresolved_added: The Summary says probability of misclassification, but the image and semantic tracks are not calibrated probabilities.
The 53.09% unlabeled and 0.672% positive figures need exact denominators and row filters.
A zero-information prior of 0.5 is not a population prevalence estimate.
Limited WSDA resources are not quantified as labor, delay, travel or cost.
Filtering unclear images by hand can remove hard but real positive cases.
Eyeball-positive seed labels lack annotation agreement and independent validation.
Majority undersampling and augmentation can change deployment prevalence and leak duplicate images across splits.
Stochastic saturation/value augmentation is described as not fixed, so exact reproducibility is absent.
The 2019 Vancouver nest is removed by geographic scope, but it may carry useful introduction information.
Missing or 1899 dates are removed without reporting counts or sensitivity.
Treating an upload as the reported insect ignores wrong-image and duplicate-image possibilities.
The boat introduction route is assumed rather than estimated.
The mean of 2019 positive points is treated as the initial nest without origin uncertainty.
Winter absence and the 121W Cascade cutoff are hard biological gates without validation.
The equal 0.5 prior is reused for missing channels without calibration.
K-Means flattens images and discards spatial structure.
Far initial centroids and stopping behavior are described without seed or convergence tolerance.
K selection metrics are based on eyeball labels, not a sealed validation set.
The ordered priorities do not specify how accuracy, FP and variance are traded when no k dominates.
k=17 pseudo-label performance is not checked on expert-held-out labels.
P(TN)=0.5833 and P(FN)=0.4167 use a denominator that is not a standard calibration definition and appear to omit FP/TP.
The algorithm assigns all images in the selected cluster positive and non-selected images negative after a coarse correction.
Pseudo-label errors are then used as CNN training labels, creating confirmation bias.
CNN downsampling to two-thirds changes the class prior; no deployment recalibration is shown.
`b0=log(TP/TN)` uses confusion counts from an earlier pseudo-label process rather than an independent prevalence estimate.
Dropout 0.5 is called common practice but no ablation is shown.
The CNN architecture, optimizer, learning rate, random seed and checkpoint rule are not fully frozen.
Binary cross-entropy is described as a probability loss, but output calibration is not evaluated.
Semantic phrases receive equal 0.05 weights despite different specificity and frequency.
Keyword extraction misses synonyms, negation, word order and unusual civilian descriptions.
Month-dependent signs are hand-coded and may capture reporting effort or seasonality instead of biology.
The semantic score can leave a narrow discrete grid and its clipping/normalization is not described.
The Fisher model requires c, K and r estimates that the current PositiveID data cannot identify.
Literature-derived c=9.74, K=1, r=1.35 are not Washington-specific estimates.
The worst-case c=30 and multiple port introductions are stress assumptions, not probabilities.
The maximum-interest region is explicitly recommendation-only, but later maps can be mistaken for model probability.
The claim that outside bounds probability is zero/one depends on hard geographic assumptions and possible intentional transport.
The unification equation's latitude/longitude condition is visually easy to transpose and inconsistent in prose notation.
The spatial override sets misclassification to 1 without an exception or confidence transition.
Missing-track branches combine scores with reliability quantities whose calibration and independence are unproven.
Clamping p to [0,1] does not make it a valid probability.
`P_images(TN)` is described as tracked during CNN training but its exact estimator is not defined.
`P_notes(TN)` uses Negative labels and a mean-plus-standard-deviation split that can be circular.
The three score populations are not independent because unlabeled pseudo-labels feed the model.
Mean/std priority intervals have no cost, capacity or false-negative derivation.
The exact cutoffs 0.503735... and 0.851353... are not robust to resampling or calibration drift.
A single GlobalID walkthrough demonstrates routing, not error rate or operational savings.
Low priority means lower estimated misclassification, not a verified negative.
The 30 km/two-season eradication condition ignores detection probability, search intensity and unreported nests.
“All reported sightings low” can be satisfied by no reports at all.
Applying the eradication rule only after unverified data are parsed creates a moving evidence set.
The 30 km circle is based on a stress spread scale, not a validated dispersal distribution.
Three-fold confusion matrices reuse augmented/pseudo-labeled images unless group splits are enforced.
The sensitivity conclusion uses maximum TP/TN differences but omits confidence intervals and statistical tests.
TP differs up to 6.06%, which is not negligible for a rare target despite the “largely insensitive” wording.
The negative set has large score variance and outliers, directly undermining a single eradication cutoff.
No target precision, recall, PR curve, calibration curve or cost-weighted metric is reported.
More PositiveID data are proposed as a repair, but data acquisition bias is not discussed.
A sentiment neural net is proposed without a labeled language corpus or evaluation plan.
Annual spatial updates lack a release gate, rollback, drift alarm and ownership.
The model's “real time” claim ignores CNN inference, preprocessing and queue latency measurements.
The memo's two-track explanation omits some three-track spatial details from the body.
The memo describes probabilities on a 0-1 scale without preserving calibration caveats.
County recommendations are based on unverified/unprocessed scores with no uncertainty or workload estimate.
Form redesign suggestions are reasonable but not tested for compliance, accessibility or selection bias.
The memo says all priority levels deserve some review but gives no minimum staffing or sampling rule.
The low-priority-not-false caveat is stronger than the Summary's simple eradication sentence and should govern.
Reference-based claims about climate, habitat and insect behavior are not sensitivity-tested locally.
The source uses “accuracy” in multiple local meanings: K-Means selection, CNN output and probability-band separation.
The paper's strongest contribution is the decision interface and explicit model downgrade; it must not be learned as proof of eradication or calibrated semi-supervised accuracy.
